newsitem.title: FRANCE: Spain's Aznar against delaying EMU or easing terms.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Aznar against delaying EMU or easing terms.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said in a newspaper interview on Saturday he was against delays to the planned start of European Monetary Union in January 1999 or softening the Maastricht convergence criteria.
"I am not in favour of softening the criteria nor of changing the calendar (for monetary union)," Aznar told the afternoon daily Le Monde.
He said it was paramount that a majority of countries met the convergence criteria in time to avoid a split within Europe.
Aznar also said he was determined to see Spain among he first round of countries joining the single currency launch, having pushed for a restrictive budget to achieve that goal.
"Our electoral pledge was to make all necessary efforts to position Spain for the single currency...I do not want Spain to miss that opportunity," he said
Aznar and French president Jacques Chirac will meet for talks on November 4-5 in Toulouse.
